title: Diagonal language escapes the time class
statement: Let $S$ be a diagonal simulator for a function $\Phi:\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $g,T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every natural number $A$ and every threshold $N$, there is some $n\ge N$ such that $A\Phi(T(n),n)\le g(n)$. Then the language consisting of inputs on which the simulator's machine does not compute the one-symbol output $1$ within $g(n)$ steps, where $n$ is the input length, does not belong to $\mathrm{DTIME}(T)$.
hypotheses_covered: For every $A,N\in\mathbb{N}$, some $n\ge N$ satisfies $A\Phi(T(n),n)\le g(n)$
